title: Bayes' theorem as a named reweighting identity
dek: P(θ|y) ∝ f(y|θ)P(θ). Wikipedia identity. Parameter-Bayesian practice stays on stats-bayesian.
story: Bayes' theorem on Wikipedia is an identity about reweighting: the posterior is the likelihood times the prior, normalised by the marginal. Nothing in the identity tells you which prior is honest, or whether θ is a parameter or a disease indicator.

stats-bayesian already treats θ as a parameter. stats-predictive-values already treats disease as the unknown. This card is the shared identity both plates rest on, so searches for 'Bayes theorem' do not invent a third protocol.
Diagnostic-test Bayes (prevalence × LR) is the same identity with a binary θ. Do not mix that with MCMC on a hierarchical GLM in one sentence without saying you changed θ.
deep: m(y) = ∫ f(y|θ)p(θ)dθ is the hard part; conjugacy and MCMC are ways to avoid staring at it.
A likelihood ratio in diagnostic testing is not Wilks' Λ.
NIST does not replace a prior with a vibes-based 'uninformative' slogan — Jeffreys has its own card.

visual.caption: Identity as a flow: prior and likelihood in, posterior out. Diagnostic versus parameter uses are different downstream plates.

steps.title: The denominator needs the false-positive path
